questions.question: 1. If a node in a binary search tree has two children, how can its value be deleted using its inorder successor?

answers.a: Swap its value with the rightmost node in its left subtree, then delete the original node without reconnecting the tree.
answers.b: Swap its value with the leftmost node in its right subtree, then delete that successor node.
answers.c: Swap its value with the rightmost node in its left subtree, then delete the original node position without further changes.
answers.d: Swap its value with the leftmost node in its right subtree, then delete the root of the entire tree.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Although the rightmost node of the left subtree can be used as an inorder predecessor, the described deletion does not correctly complete the replacement process.
explanations.b: Correct. The leftmost node of the right subtree is the inorder successor. Its value can replace the target value, after which the successor node can be deleted.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Replacing the target value requires deleting the node containing the replacement value rather than simply removing the original node position.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The root of the entire tree is unrelated to the inorder successor unless it happens to be the relevant node.

questions.question: 2. If a node in a BST has only one child to the right and no left child, how can the node be deleted?

answers.a: Swap its value with the leftmost node in its right subtree, then delete that node.
answers.b: Connect the node's parent directly to its right child, then delete the node.
answers.c: Delete the node and set all pointers to null.
answers.d: Swap its value with the root of the tree and then delete the root.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Swapping with another node is unnecessary when the target has only one child.
explanations.b: Correct. The parent's link can bypass the target node and point directly to its right child, preserving the subtree.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Removing the node without reconnecting its child would disconnect the remaining subtree.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The root is not involved in the standard deletion of a node with one child.

questions.question: 3. In a real BST, deletion takes $O(\log n)$ time when the tree is balanced. Assume an oracle can search and compute the minimum or maximum of a subtree in $O(1)$ time. What is the time complexity of an optimal deletion algorithm using this oracle?

explanations.a: Correct. The oracle provides the required search and successor/predecessor information in constant time, and the remaining pointer updates require only a constant number of operations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This complexity would still include logarithmic traversal work that the oracle has eliminated.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The deletion procedure does not involve a repeated logarithmic reduction that would produce this complexity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Deletion does not require visiting every node of the tree.

questions.question: 4. When deleting a leaf node from a BST, what should be done?

answers.a: Replace it with its inorder successor.
answers.b: Replace it with its inorder predecessor.
answers.c: Remove the node and update its parent's corresponding child pointer.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A leaf has no children, so replacement by another node is unnecessary.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A leaf does not require predecessor replacement because it has no child subtree to preserve.
explanations.c: Correct. Since a leaf has no children, it can be removed and the parent's corresponding pointer can be set appropriately.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The root does not need to be involved when deleting an ordinary leaf.

questions.question: 5. Which node can be used to replace a BST node that has two children while preserving the BST ordering property?

answers.b: The inorder successor or inorder predecessor
answers.d: Any node at the same level

explanations.a: Incorrect. An arbitrary leaf may not have a key value suitable for preserving the BST ordering.
explanations.b: Correct. The inorder successor or inorder predecessor has a key value that can replace the deleted node while maintaining the BST ordering.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The root is not generally the appropriate replacement node.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Nodes at the same level do not necessarily have an appropriate key value for replacement.

questions.question: 6. Which of the following cases is generally the simplest BST deletion case?

answers.a: Deleting a node with two children
answers.b: Deleting the root when it has two children
answers.d: Deleting a node whose successor has a child

explanations.a: Incorrect. A node with two children requires additional replacement and restructuring steps.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Deleting a root with two children requires handling the two-subtree case.
explanations.c: Correct. A leaf has no children, so it can be removed by updating the appropriate parent pointer.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A successor with a child requires additional pointer adjustment after replacement.

questions.question: 7. When deleting a BST node using its inorder successor, where is that successor located?

answers.a: At the leftmost node of the target's right subtree
answers.b: At the rightmost node of the target's right subtree
answers.c: At the leftmost node of the target's left subtree
answers.d: At the root of the entire tree

explanations.a: Correct. The inorder successor is the smallest key greater than the target, which is found at the leftmost node of the target's right subtree.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The rightmost node of the right subtree represents a larger key than the successor.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The left subtree contains keys smaller than the target and is associated with finding the predecessor.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The root is not generally the inorder successor.

questions.question: 8. After replacing a BST node with its inorder successor, why is deleting the successor usually simpler than deleting the original two-child node?

answers.a: The successor is always the root.
answers.b: The successor is guaranteed to have no parent.
answers.c: The successor has no larger keys in the tree.
answers.d: The inorder successor has no left child and therefore has at most one child.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The successor can occur at many different positions in the tree.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The successor is normally a descendant of the node being deleted and therefore has a parent unless it is the root itself.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The absence of larger keys is not the reason that successor deletion is simpler.
explanations.d: Correct. Because the successor is the leftmost node in the right subtree, it has no left child and therefore can have at most one child.

questions.question: 9. If a BST node has only a left child, what is the appropriate structural action when deleting that node?

answers.a: Connect the parent directly to the left child.
answers.c: Replace the node with the root of the tree.
answers.d: Always rotate the tree before deletion.

explanations.a: Correct. The parent can bypass the deleted node and point directly to its left child, preserving the remaining subtree.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The left subtree contains valid BST nodes and should not be discarded.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Replacing the node with the root is unrelated to the one-child deletion case.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A rotation is not inherently required when deleting a node with one child from an ordinary BST.
